$comment: ELF64 SHARED LIBRARY (ET_DYN, .so) for aarch64 Linux -- c171 conformance (the arm64 sibling of elf64-x86_64-linux-dyn, D-LK-ELF-DYN-AARCH64-FLAVOR). CONFIG-ONLY: the `src/link/format/elf.cpp` writer is machine-parameterized -- `elf.type = dyn` routes to the SAME `encodeElfExecDynamic` substrate, whose arm64 arms ALREADY EXIST (the ET_DYN dispatch machine-guard admits machine 183; `relativeRelocTypeFor(183)` = R_AARCH64_RELATIVE = 1027; `globDatTypeFor(183)` = R_AARCH64_GLOB_DAT = 1025; `emitArm64PltStub()` is the 16-byte ADRP+LDR+BR GOT-indirect stub the aarch64 EXEC already uses for its libc `exit` PLT). So this needs NO writer code, only this schema. The dyn divergences (e_type=ET_DYN, e_entry=0, no PT_PHDR/PT_INTERP/.interp, base-0 VAs the loader slides, real-named .dynsym EXPORTS findable via .hash, R_AARCH64_RELATIVE for internal absolute data slots, got-indirect extern data) are identical to the x86_64 .so; only the machine (183 vs 62), the reloc rows (arm64 vs x86_64), and the writer's per-machine RELATIVE/GLOB_DAT/PLT-stub selection differ. A FOREIGN toolchain consumes the output: `aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc main.c -L. -lfoo` links against the DSS-emitted libfoo.so and the program runs under qemu-aarch64 / on the ubuntu-24.04-arm CI leg. Differs from elf64-aarch64-linux-exec in: `elf.type` (dyn vs exec), NO `interpreter` (a .so is loaded by an already-running ld.so; validate() rejects one here), text `virtualAddress` = pageAlign (base-0 image; validate() pins the equality), NO `entryPoint`/`processExit`/`entryCallingConvention`/`processArgs` (a .so has no process entry -- the PIE-executable sibling is exactly ET_DYN plus that entry machinery), `dataImportBinding` got-indirect (copy relocations are exec-only ELF), NO `tlsAccess` and NO tdata/tbss rows (TLS in a .so needs the general-dynamic model -- D-LK-DYN-TLS-MODEL; every thread_local fails loud at the MIR->LIR gate / linker section gate), `artifactProfiles` ["lib"].
$stackReserveUnsupportedReasonComment: D-SQLITE-PE64-FULL-TIER-STACK-DEPTH: ELF has NO image field for a stack SIZE on ANY flavor -- PT_GNU_STACK encodes stack EXECUTABILITY, not size. The kernel sizes the initial thread's stack from the process limit (`ulimit -s` / setrlimit RLIMIT_STACK) and further threads from pthread_attr_setstacksize, so nothing the linker writes can change it. A `stackReserve` / `--stack-reserve` request is therefore REFUSED with that remedy rather than silently dropped -- which is also why the sqlite full tier passes on Linux (8 MiB by default) and overflowed on Windows at 1 MiB.
$dataModelComment: Same LP64 identity as the aarch64 exec/rel siblings (64-bit Linux).
$headerNameMatchingComment: D-PP-HEADER-CASE-INSENSITIVE-PE: Linux/POSIX header names are matched BYTE-EXACT -- `#include <Stdio.h>` does NOT name `stdio.h`, and a conforming toolchain must reject it. REQUIRED closed-enum field: the loader rejects a missing or unknown value. DSS performs the comparison ITSELF (core/types/include_path_resolve.cpp) rather than calling fs::exists and inheriting the BUILD HOST's convention -- without that, an elf target built on Windows/macOS silently ACCEPTED `<Stdio.h>` and emitted a real object (MEASURED 2026-08-04).
$cSymbolDecorationComment: D-FFI-CMANGLING-RULE-NOT-CONFIG-DRIVEN: System V / ELF applies NO decoration to a C identifier -- the linker-visible name IS the identifier. MEASURED 2026-08-06 (`nm -D /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6`, WSL Ubuntu): glibc exports `exit@@GLIBC_2.2.5`, `printf@@GLIBC_2.2.5` and `fstat64@@GLIBC_2.33` under exactly their C spellings. THE SAME COMMAND IS ALSO WHY `none` IS A POSITIVE ANSWER AND NOT AN ABSENCE: `_exit@@GLIBC_2.2.5` is exported TOO and is a DIFFERENT FUNCTION -- POSIX `_exit(2)`, which does NOT flush stdio -- so a format that wrongly claimed `leading-underscore` would not merely produce an ugly name, it would silently bind every `exit` to the non-flushing wrapper and lose buffered output. This key is the single owner of a fact that previously had TWO: the closed C++ table `kCManglingRules` (src/ffi/mangling/c_mangle.cpp, keyed on ObjectFormatKind) and, redundantly, a literal encoding in the descriptors themselves -- the macho64-*-exec files spell `processExit.importMangledName` as `_exit` while their elf/pe siblings spell it `exit`. Two owners in two languages, with nothing forcing them to agree. RED-ON-DISABLE, stated precisely for the tier that exists today (MEASURED 2026-08-06 by actually removing the key from a shipped file and running the suite): DELETE this key and the format is REFUSED AT LOAD -- TWO errors at /cSymbolDecoration, one C_MissingField from the loader and one from ObjectFormatData::validate(), which loadFromText runs before returning -- so every test and example that loads this format goes red, naming the file. CHANGING the value is now an equally REAL lever, and this sentence was corrected the moment it became true: before step C4 the engine still read a C++ table and the value here changed no emitted binary. C4 landed (same cycle, TF-C122), and the effect is MEASURED 2026-08-06 -- flipping macho64-arm64-darwin-exec from `leading-underscore` to `none` and RECOMPILING NOTHING made the engine emit `printf` where it had emitted `_printf`, reddening tests/ffi/test_c_mangle.cpp's SchemeIsReadFromTheShippedSchemaNotACppTable. That is the whole point of the anchor: the answer lives in this file, so editing this file changes what the compiler emits. Two further pins guard the value: tests/link/test_c_symbol_decoration.cpp asserts the per-kind answer across all 24 shipped files and cross-checks it against this family's own processExit.importMangledName.
$predefinedMacrosComment: TF-C97 (D-PP-FORMAT-DATA-MODEL-PREDEFINES): the C-visible face of this file's `dataModel` above, DERIVED FROM THAT VALUE AND NEVER FROM THIS FILE'S NAME -- the loader synthesizes no macro name and the engine performs no format-identity branch; it merges whatever rows are declared here with the language's `preprocess.predefinedMacros` and the target's `predefinedMacros`, applying `availableObjectFormats` exactly once. DECLARED ON THE FORMAT because the data model is per-(OS x format), not per-CPU: the same x86_64 target is LP64 here and LLP64 under pe64-x86_64-windows-*, so a target-side row would be wrong on one of its own formats -- which is exactly what both .target.json files say when they record `__LP64__`/`_LP64` as DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED and defer to the format. BOTH spellings, each value 1: MEASURED 2026-07-30 with `/usr/bin/clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target <triple>` (Apple clang 21.0.0), __LP64__ and _LP64 are BOTH defined as 1 on arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-linux-gnu and x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, and NEITHER is defined on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. COLLISION POLICY: a name declared by this file AND the language or target config is FATAL (C_ConflictingPredefinedMacro) -- no side silently wins. WHAT IT UNBLOCKS, MEASURED: the macOS SDK gates 234 occurrences across 91 headers on __LP64__, so without these rows DSS compiled the SDK's ILP32 arms while its own widths were LP64 (sizeof(long)==8), and $SDK/usr/include/mach/port.h:113-114 then asserted the user32 struct size 12 instead of user64's 16 -- sqlite mem1.c's three error[S0029]. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete this key and examples/c/predefined_lp64_macho stops exiting 42.
$bitFieldStrategyComment: D-CSUBSET-BITFIELD-ABI-EXACT: Linux arm64 (AAPCS64) uses the generic LSB-first bit-field allocation -- identical to SysV/GNU gnu_packed for little-endian -- same as the aarch64 ELF siblings.
$externCallDispatchComment: Same call-site shape as the exec image: the walker synthesizes a 16-byte ARM64 PLT stub (ADRP+LDR+BR through the GOT slot, GLOB_DAT eager-bound) per extern FUNCTION, and the call site is a plain direct `BL` to the stub -- pc-relative, so the code needs no fixup under the ET_DYN load slide. D-FFI-EXTERN-CALL-DISPATCH / D-LK6-8.
$weakDefinitionComment: D-CONFIG-WEAK-DEFINITION-DIALECT-NOT-DECLARED + D-LK-WEAK-DEFINITION-DIALECT-UNCONSULTED-BY-ELF-AND-MACHO-WRITERS: HOW this format spells a WEAK DEFINITION -- a symbol several translation units may define, of which the linker keeps one. ELF puts the weakness in the SYMBOL's own BINDING field: STB_WEAK (2) in the high nibble of Elf64_Sym.st_info, gABI 4.18. No section flag and no separate per-symbol flag bit is involved, which is exactly what distinguishes `symbol-binding` from COFF's `comdat` (a per-SECTION duplicate-resolution policy) and from Mach-O's `symbol-flag` (N_WEAK_DEF set ALONGSIDE an ordinary binding). Written by `stbForBinding` in src/link/format/elf.cpp. THIS IS A DIALECT ROW, NOT A CAPABILITY FLAG: it says how this format spells something it CAN express, never that it cannot -- see D-LK-PE-ALTERNATENAME-DECLARE-AND-REFUSE for why an implementation gap recorded as a format incapability is a false fact in the place most likely to be trusted later. `elf::encode` READS this key -- ONCE, covering every ELF flavor, because the alias pass reaches stbForBinding on ET_REL, ET_EXEC and ET_DYN alike -- and refuses loud on a dialect it has no encoder for, so the declaration cannot drift away from what is actually emitted. The loader additionally refuses this key at LOAD when the declared dialect is not one the resolved backend's walker writes (ObjectFormatBackend::weakDefinitionDialects), so a mis-declaration fails at its source rather than at the first weak definition.
$dataImportBindingComment: c150 (D-LK1-4 + D-LK-EXTERN-DATA-IMPORT): extern library DATA objects bind GOT-INDIRECT in a shared library -- the walker reserves a GOT slot per imported object and emits R_AARCH64_GLOB_DAT against it; ld.so writes the object's address into the slot and the GotIndirect lowering reads it. The exec sibling declares the SAME value now: copy-relocation was DELETED from the vocabulary (D-LK-ELF-COPY-RELOC-CLAIMS-ONE-NAME-OF-AN-ALIAS-SET — it split an aliased libc object silently), so there is nothing a .so has to be protected from here; the loader's closed-enum reject refuses the spelling on ANY flavour.
$supportedDataSectionsComment: rodata (read-only, R+X PT_LOAD #1 -- reloc-FREE items only: a reloc-bearing rodata item would need a load-time write into a read-only page, D-LK-DYN-RODATA-ITEM-RELOC fails loud), data (mutable initialized globals, R+W PT_LOAD #2), bss (zero-init, NOBITS tail of PT_LOAD #2), relro (reloc-bearing CONST data, c145 -- merged into `.data` by the dynamic arm so its R_AARCH64_RELATIVE slots land in writable pages). NO tdata/tbss: thread-locals in a shared library need the general-dynamic TLS model (D-LK-DYN-TLS-MODEL, not implemented); the linker's pre-walker gate rejects them loudly by this set's absence.
$artifactProfilesComment: This format SERVES the shared-library profile (plan 06 AP3). The cli profile is NOT served (a .so is not a runnable console binary). ★ `module` JOINED THIS SET 2026-08-15 (plan 06 §5.1 B.12, as CORRECTED): a module IS a library, so it is served by every format that serves `lib` or `staticlib` and by nothing else. `artifactProfile` says what a project builds ITSELF as; `DependencyComposition` says how it is CONSUMED (`module` is SourceMerge — a consumer takes its SOURCES and ignores its artifact). Those are orthogonal, so a module builds standalone like any other library and the static-vs-dynamic choice is made by the `<target>:<format>` spec the author writes in `targets[]`, exactly as it already is for `lib` vs `staticlib` — no new rule and no engine change.

elf.$comment: Elf64_Ehdr identity for an arm64 shared library. type = ET_DYN (3). e_entry = 0 (no process entry). machine = 183 (EM_AARCH64). NO interpreter (validate() rejects one on dyn). bindNow = true: eager binding, DT_FLAGS_1 = DF_1_NOW + R_AARCH64_GLOB_DAT in .rela.dyn -- the same v1 stance as the exec image.

sections.$comment: Executable code. virtualAddress = 4096 = elf.pageAlign, PINNED by validate(): ET_DYN VAs are BASE-RELATIVE (the loader slides the whole image), and the walker computes baseImageVa = text.virtualAddress - pageAlign, so the equality makes the image base 0 BY CONSTRUCTION -- the gcc .so convention. sh_flags = SHF_ALLOC|SHF_EXECINSTR (6).
sections.name: .text

sections.$comment: Read-only initialized data (string literals, reloc-free const globals). Folded into the R+X PT_LOAD #1 after .text. virtualAddress = 0 -- computed. A reloc-BEARING const global goes to relro instead (c145): RELATIVE fixups must land in writable pages.
sections.name: .rodata

sections.$comment: Writable initialized data. R+W PT_LOAD #2 (W^X preserved). virtualAddress = 0 -- computed.
sections.name: .data

sections.$comment: Zero-initialized data. SHT_NOBITS (8); memsz-only tail of PT_LOAD #2. virtualAddress = 0 -- computed.
sections.name: .bss

sections.$comment: Symbol table (debugger support; the LOADER reads .dynsym, which the walker emits unconditionally on this arm). sh_entsize = 24.
sections.name: .symtab

relocations.$comment: 26-bit PC-relative branch-with-link (BL) -- the extern-call reloc on a PLT stub. Legal in ET_DYN `.text` (pc-relative, no DT_TEXTREL). kind = 1 matches arm64.target.json's `call26` row. ★ `isCall` (D-LK-MACHO-ISDATA-NO-CALL-SIGNAL, 2026-08-20): this wire relocation can ONLY target executable code, so an object reader that meets an undefined extern through it has PROVEN the extern is a function rather than a data object -- the only classification signal a symbol-name-only reference offers. It is declared HERE, on the format row, and not derived from the target's formula, because a formula describes ARITHMETIC and not ROLE: `S + A - P` is the identical arithmetic for a call and for a PC-relative data reference, so the x86_64 target's `linear` is honest and simply carries no role, while aarch64's `aarch64_call26` looked like a role only because that CPU's branch has its own instruction encoding. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-20: every macho64-x86_64 archive member calling any library function was unreadable for exactly this reason while the arm64 sibling read the same source cleanly. The target document cannot carry it -- it is PER-CPU and shared with ELF, where the same `rel32` genuinely serves data references too.
relocations.name: R_AARCH64_CALL26

relocations.$comment: ADRP page-base pc-relative (high 21 bits) -- data address computation. Legal in `.text` (pc-relative). kind = 2 = arm64.target.json's `adr_prel_pg_hi21`.
relocations.name: R_AARCH64_ADR_PREL_PG_HI21

relocations.$comment: ADD low-12 absolute (no check) -- the pair with ADRP for a full address. kind = 3 = `add_abs_lo12_nc`.
relocations.name: R_AARCH64_ADD_ABS_LO12_NC

relocations.$comment: abs64 -- legal in DATA items only on this arm: the walker patches the slot with the base-relative value AND emits an R_AARCH64_RELATIVE (1027) row for it (the load slide completes the address). kind = 4 = `abs64`.
relocations.name: R_AARCH64_ABS64
